title: DNS Control rule resource over the API

checks.do: Whether an update sends every field, since a PUT replaces the rule and the MCP update tool does not read it first.
Which spelling of the Web EUN flag a client sends, since the clients differ.
Whether a protocols value is one the Go struct documents, since the Python docstring lists fewer.

endpoint.statement: DNS rules use the dedicated endpoint `/zia/api/v1/firewallDnsRules`, separate from Firewall Filtering.

update-is-put.statement: Updating a DNS rule is a PUT full replacement, not a patch.

quotes: (*FirewallDNSRules, error) { resp, err := service.Client.UpdateWithPut(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("%s/%d", firewallDnsRulesEndpoint, ruleID), *rules)
"""Update a ZIA Cloud Firewall DNS rule (write, PUT-replace). Activate after."""

mcp-update-no-readback.statement: The MCP update tool builds its payload from the supplied fields and sends it straight to the SDK `update_rule`; it does not read the existing rule first.
mcp-update-no-readback.conditions: Rests on reading the tool: no get call appears before update_rule in the function. The omission semantics of build_rule_payload were not read.

enabled-to-state.statement: The Python SDK converts the `enabled` boolean to the wire field `state` with `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`.

protocols-enum.statement: The `protocols` values documented in the Go struct are `ANY_RULE`, `SMRULEF_CASCADING_ALLOWED`, `TCP_RULE`, `UDP_RULE`, `DOHTTPS_RULE`; the Python docstring gives only TCP, UDP, DOHTTPS as examples.

zpa-ip-group-always-sent.statement: In Go, `zpaIpGroup` has no `omitempty`, so it is serialized even when nil, unlike most fields on the struct.

python-edns-type.statement: The Python model assigns `edns_ecs_object` twice, first as a `ResourceReference` and then overwrites it with `CommonBlocks`, so the effective parse type is `CommonBlocks`.

python-id-wrapping.statement: The Python SDK's request-side id remapping list does not include `dns_gateway`, `zpa_ip_group` or `edns_ecs_object`, so a scalar id given for them is sent as-is rather than wrapped as `{id: ...}`, while the response parser reads them back as objects.
python-id-wrapping.conditions: Rests on the absence of the three keys from reformat_params in zscaler/utils.py, found by searching that list; the transform's behavior for unlisted keys was not re-read.

ansible-uses-python.statement: The ZIA Ansible module passes `is_web_eun_enabled` into the Python SDK's `update_rule`, so it inherits the Python wire spelling.

go-web-eun-omitempty.statement: Go emits `isWebEUNEnabled` with `omitempty`, so an explicit false is not sent.

recorded-uppercase-eun.statement: Recorded Python integration responses from the DNS rules endpoint carry the key as `isWebEUNEnabled`.

web-eun-key.summary: Spelling of the Web EUN wire key

quotes: Fixed mispelled attribute `isWebEunEnabled` to the expected API value `isWebEUNEnabled`

positions.says: The API value is isWebEUNEnabled; Go was fixed to that in 3.8.44.
The Python request dictionary emits isWebEunEnabled.

web-eun-key.impact: Python and Ansible callers may send a key the API does not recognise, so Web EUN writes may be rejected or ignored (the Go changelog says the misspelling caused payload errors on POST/PUT); compare by reading the rule back.

web-eun-false.title: What an omitted or explicit false Web EUN does on update
web-eun-false.blocks: knowing whether Go can clear Web EUN and whether Python/Ansible spelling takes effect
web-eun-false.detail: Go omits false, Python emits a differently cased key. Whether omission preserves an existing true or clears it is not shown; see also the general rule-update gap in zia.sdk-go.write-encoding. Needs a live update test; do not infer equivalence between the clients.
